subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding filename decoder live, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects core media, bundled channel plugins, plugin-facing reuse, and dependency ownership; automation should not choose that API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use a plugin-safe shared decoder
options.body: Put the decoder in media-core or an explicitly exported plugin-safe SDK boundary, then refresh the existing candidate or a replacement around that single shared helper.

options.title: Keep narrow channel repairs
options.body: Treat the existing Feishu fixes as sufficient for now and defer broader multi-encoding support until concrete non-Feishu channel reports arrive.

options.title: Require broader live repros first
options.body: Keep this issue open but ask for real GB18030, Shift-JIS, EUC-KR, or non-Feishu failures before approving a shared utility.

recommendation.title: Use a plugin-safe shared decoder
recommendation.body: Put the decoder in media-core or an explicitly exported plugin-safe SDK boundary, then refresh the existing candidate or a replacement around that single shared helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Feishu filename work plus release/media-core context make this the strongest available owner for the API-boundary choice.
